questions.question: If a wooden chair, a metal coin, and a plastic cup are left in a classroom overnight, what can we say about their temperatures in the morning?
options: The metal coin will be much colder than the wooden chair and plastic cup.
All three objects will have reached the exact same temperature as the room.
The plastic cup will have warmed up to be hotter than the room's temperature.
The wood and plastic will be warmer than the room, while the metal will be colder.

questions.question: What happens to the overall volume of a solid or liquid when it is heated?
options: It expands because its particles take up more space as they separate.
It contracts because the particles get closer together.
It remains exactly the same size because the mass does not change.
It expands because the individual particles grow larger in size.

questions.question: When a hot mug of tea is left on a desk, why do the particles of the tea begin to move less quickly over time?
options: They lose energy as they transfer it to the surrounding air particles.
They absorb coldness from the surrounding air particles.
The particles of the tea stick together and stop moving entirely.
The tea particles evaporate, leaving only stationary particles behind.

questions.question: Under which condition will a hot drink cool down at the fastest rate?
options: When the temperature difference between the drink and the air is very small.
When the drink is at the exact same temperature as the surrounding air.
When there is a very large temperature difference between the drink and the air.
When the drink is placed in a room that is slightly warmer than the drink.

questions.question: If you want to heat equal masses of different substances to reach the exact same target temperature, what must be true?
options: They will all require the exact same amount of heating.
Different substances will require different amounts of heating.
Only the substance with the lowest density will need heating.
The heating time will only depend on the volume of the container.

questions.question: What does a higher specific heat capacity tell us about 1 kg of a substance at a particular temperature?
options: It contains more energy in its thermal store compared to a substance with a lower specific heat capacity.
It contains less energy in its thermal store because it is a better thermal conductor.
It is able to change state much more quickly than other substances.
Its particles move in a single, fixed direction rather than randomly.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true about the directions in which particles move in solids, liquids, and gases?
options: The directions of movement are completely random in all three states of matter.
Particles in solids move in neat circles, while only gas particles move randomly.
Liquid particles move only downwards due to gravity, while gas particles move randomly.
Solid particles do not move at all, so they have no direction of movement.

questions.question: Compare two identical copper blocks, where Block A is at 80 degrees Celsius and Block B is at 20 degrees Celsius. Which block has more energy in its thermal store?
options: Block B, because cooler objects have more stable thermal energy.
Block A, because it is at a higher temperature.
Both blocks have the same energy because they are made of identical material and mass.
Neither block has any thermal energy because copper is a metal conductor.

questions.question: You have two buckets of water, both at exactly 40 degrees Celsius. Bucket X contains 10 litres of water, and Bucket Y contains 2 litres of water. Which has more energy in its thermal store?
options: Bucket Y, because the energy is more concentrated in a smaller volume.
Both have the exact same energy because their temperatures are identical.
Bucket X, because it contains more particles of the substance.
Neither bucket has thermal energy because 40 degrees Celsius is below the boiling point.

questions.question: To obtain an accurate temperature measurement when using a glass thermometer, how should you position your eyes?
options: Look down at the thermometer from directly above the tube.
Keep your eye level with the top of the coloured liquid inside the thermometer.
Look up at the thermometer from a low angle to see the base of the bulb.
Tilt the thermometer at a 45-degree angle to read the scale from the side.

questions.question: If you mix a cup of hot water at 80 degrees Celsius with a cup of cold water at 10 degrees Celsius, what will the final temperature of the mixture be?
options: Exactly 0 degrees Celsius, as the hot and cold water cancel each other out.
Higher than 80 degrees Celsius because the particles collide and generate extra heat.
Cooler than the hot water but warmer than the cold water.
Exactly 90 degrees Celsius, which is the sum of both temperatures.

questions.question: When 500 ml of hot water is mixed with 100 ml of cold water, how does the final temperature compare to the starting temperatures of each?
options: It will be closer to the temperature of the cold water.
It will be closer to the temperature of the hot water because there was more of it.
It will be exactly halfway between the hot and cold temperatures regardless of the volumes.
It will be colder than both starting temperatures.

questions.question: How is thermal energy transferred through a good thermal conductor at the particle level?
options: Vibrating particles quickly cause the particles next to them to vibrate as well.
The particles flow from the hot end to the cold end in a large current.
The particles stop vibrating completely to let heat pass through the gaps.
The particles shrink, allowing heat waves to pass freely between them.

questions.question: Why does the temperature along a thermal insulator increase very slowly when it is heated?
options: Because the particles in an insulator are already moving at the speed of light.
Because it is difficult for vibrating particles in an insulator to cause neighbouring particles to vibrate.
Because insulators contain no particles, so there is nothing to vibrate.
Because the particles in an insulator absorb heat and destroy it.

questions.question: Why do materials that contain trapped air, like wool or bubble wrap, make excellent thermal insulators?
options: Because gases are extremely poor thermal conductors.
Because trapped air acts as a vacuum that contains no particles.
Because air particles vibrate much faster than metal particles when heated.
Because gases are excellent thermal conductors that distribute heat away.

questions.question: What is the effect of wrapping a cold canned drink in a thermal insulator?
options: It will warm the drink up rapidly because insulators generate heat.
It keeps the cold drink cool by slowing down the transfer of heat from the surroundings.
It makes the cold drink freeze solid because insulators lower the temperature.
It has no effect because insulators only work on hot objects like hot drinks.
